concept.name: Perpetual basis
concept.definition: The perpetual basis is the price difference between a perpetual futures contract and the underlying spot (index) price, typically expressed as a percentage; the funding mechanism exists to keep this basis mean-reverting around zero.
concept.intuition: It is how far the tail (perp) wags from the dog (spot): positive when perp buyers pay a premium, negative when perps trade at a discount.
concept.mechanics: Basis = perp price − index price (or (perp/index) − 1). Unlike dated futures, whose basis converges at expiry, perp basis is anchored continuously by funding: a persistent positive basis raises funding, charging longs and attracting cash-and-carry arbitrage (buy spot, short perp, collect funding) that compresses it. Binance's premium index operationalizes the basis using impact bid/ask prices rather than last trade.
concept.formula: Basis % = (perp price / spot index − 1) × 100; annualized carry ≈ average funding rate × 3 × 365 (8h interval).
concept.failure_modes: In liquidation cascades or index outages, the basis can gap violently (perp trading far below spot) before funding arbitrage restores it; basis also embeds the premium index's order-book sampling, so thin books give noisy readings.
concept.misconceptions: A wide positive basis is not a free carry trade — funding can flip or spike, and execution of both legs has costs and margin risk. Perp basis is not a forecast of spot direction; it primarily reflects positioning imbalance.
concept.example: BTC spot index at $100,000 while the perp prints $100,500: basis +0.5%; funding turns positive, and arbitrageurs shorting the perp against spot longs collect ~0.01% per 8h until the premium closes.

citations.source: Binance Support - Introduction to Binance Futures Funding Rates
